alt: A group over-represented in crime statistics raises two questions: do they commit more crime (strain, status frustration, relative deprivation, masculinity) or are they more likely to be caught, recorded and punished (police targeting, labelling, institutional racism, chivalry, white-collar crime handled outside courts)?
caption: Separate offending from being caught and recorded.

alt: Patterns of recorded offending and victimisation by age, social class, gender and ethnicity, described in words.
caption: Each group has a pattern of offending and a pattern of victimisation.

alt: Society values goals such as wealth but blocks legitimate means for some, creating strain. People adapt in five ways: conformity, innovation, ritualism, retreatism and rebellion. Innovation, using crime to reach the goal, is the adaptation that explains crime.
caption: Innovation is the adaptation that leads to crime.

alt: Primary deviance becomes secondary deviance once a label, possibly a master status, is applied. Below, Stanley Cohen’s deviancy amplification spiral: media exaggeration creates folk devils, public concern, tougher control and more deviance, which the media report.
caption: Labels and media reactions can create the deviance they condemn.

alt: Carlen’s class deal and gender deal: women who gain the rewards of paid work and family life conform, while those who gain from neither are more likely to offend. Below, Heidensohn on tighter control of women, Pollak’s chivalry thesis and Messerschmidt on accomplishing masculinity.
caption: Control, deals, leniency and masculinity all help explain the gap.

alt: A table of five theories of crime with a key idea, strength and limitation each: functionalism, interactionism, Marxism, feminism and postmodernism.
caption: Every theory explains some patterns and misses others.

alt: A balance weighing socialisation and control (Heidensohn, gendered socialisation) against alternatives (chivalry thesis, Messerschmidt, Carlen, changing opportunities). The judgement: socialisation explains much, but recording and opportunity also matter.
caption: Include the statistics debate and at least one alternative explanation.
